Historical findings CASEID FILE NOTE
1) Domain context: A generic institutional records office files ordinary paperwork through standardized intake forms, assigns sequential document identifiers, routes submissions to designated review channels, logs access to physical files, and maintains dated custody registers that track the movement of records between offices.

2) What occurred: The actor presented a dated inspection report document to a designated review channel on a recorded date. The actor submitted a correspondence document bearing a financial instrument to a personal account on a recorded date. The actor altered a compliance field within the inspection file to a non-conforming value on a recorded date. The actor modified the signature block of the inspection file to an unauthorized signature on a recorded date. The actor removed two pages from the physical inspection file and recorded the gap in a custody log entry on a recorded date.

3) Materials/access observed: The actor used a named administrative account to access the inspection file record. The actor possessed a financial instrument with an account number and routing code. The actor handled the physical inspection file containing the original signature and the dated report pages. The actor accessed the custody register entry for the file location.

4) Indicators & artifacts: The altered compliance field value conflicts with the original inspection report document. The financial instrument amount matches the quoted repair cost in a dated estimate document. The unauthorized signature does not match the authorized signatory list. The custody log shows an unexplained gap for the removed pages. The administrative account access log shows after-hours access to the inspection file. The correspondence document was sent to a personal account rather than the institutional escrow channel.
